source.text: וְזֹ֣את הַבְּרָכָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בֵּרַ֥ךְ מֹשֶׁ֛ה אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לִפְנֵ֖י מוֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] the blessing which blessed Moses, [the] man of the God, the sons of Israel before his death.

en.L: And this [is] the blessing with which Moses the man of God blessed the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel before his death.
en.B: This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced over the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} before he died.
en.R: Moses, the man of God, gave this blessing to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} before he died.

decisions.choice: the man of God: a title for a prophet, one who speaks God's word
decisions.reason: The title is given to prophets and to those God sends with his message (Joshua 14:6; 1 Samuel 9:6-10; 1 Kings 17:24). Here it is used of Moses for the first time; Psalm 90 is headed with the same words. It names his office, not only his character.

decisions.choice: the blessing before his death: a father's last words over his family
decisions.reason: As Jacob blessed his sons before he died (Genesis 49:1-28; compare 27:1-4), Moses blesses the tribes. Such last words were more than a wish: they were spoken in God's name and looked ahead to each tribe's future. The poem itself runs from verse 2 to verse 29; this verse is its heading, in prose.

decisions.choice: pronounced over
decisions.reason: Balanced says the blessing was "pronounced over" the people, so that "blessing ... blessed" does not stand side by side. Literal keeps the repeated root.

decisions.choice: no line breaks in this verse
decisions.reason: This verse is the narrator's prose heading, so it is not set in lines. The poem that follows is.

source.text: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֞ה מִסִּינַ֥י בָּא֙ וְזָרַ֤ח מִשֵּׂעִיר֙ לָ֔מוֹ הוֹפִ֨יעַ֙ מֵהַ֣ר פָּארָ֔ן וְאָתָ֖ה מֵרִבְבֹ֣ת קֹ֑דֶשׁ מִֽימִינ֕וֹ אֵ֥שׁ דָּ֖ת לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Yahweh from Sinai came, and dawned from Seir upon them; he shone forth from [the] mountain of Paran, and he came from myriads of holiness; from his right hand fire of law for them.

en.L: And he said, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came from Sinai and dawned on them from Seir; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shone forth from Mount Paran \q and came from [the] myriads of holiness; \q from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand [came] a fiery law for them.
en.B: He said: \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came from Sinai and rose like the dawn on them from Seir; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shone out from Mount Paran \q and came from among myriads of holy ones; \q from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand came a law of fire for them.
en.R: Moses said: \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came from Mount Sinai. \q Like the sunrise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came from Seir and shone from Mount Paran. \q He came from among many thousands of holy ones. \q From {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand came a fiery law for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: Sinai, Seir, Paran: the LORD's coming pictured as sunrise over the mountains of the south
decisions.reason: God's coming to his people is described like the sun rising and spreading its light from one range of hills to the next. Seir is the hill country of Edom (2:1-8), and Paran the wilderness south of Canaan (1:1; Numbers 10:12). Other old poems of God marching from the south use the same places (Judges 5:4-5; Psalm 68:8-9; Habakkuk 3:3). "Them" and "for them" are Israel, named in verses 4-5.

decisions.choice: came from the myriads of holiness: came out from among countless holy ones, the heavenly host around God
alternatives: came with myriads of holy ones
decisions.reason: The holy ones are most likely the heavenly beings who surround God (Psalm 68:18; Zechariah 14:5; Daniel 7:10). The Greek translation reads the same letters as a place, "with the myriads of Kadesh"; with one letter fewer, the Hebrew would be "Meribath-kadesh" (32:51), which would carry on the list of places in the first lines. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: a fiery law: the two words the scribes' margin note marks to be read, "fire" and "law"
alternatives: with him, angels at his right hand
decisions.reason: The consonants are written as one word in the Hebrew text, which no one knows the meaning of. The scribes' note says to read two words, "fire of law", and the source data follows that reading. The word for law, dat, is otherwise found only in books written much later (Ezra, Esther), so many find the reading doubtful. Proposals include "fire flashing" (lightning, as at Sinai, Exodus 19:16-18) and a word for mountain slopes (3:17; 4:49). The Greek translation has "angels with him at his right hand". The meaning is not certain.

decisions.choice: from his right hand: from his own power and authority
decisions.reason: The right hand is the hand of power (Exodus 15:6, 12). The law came to Israel from God himself (5:22). The same word can also mean the south, but here it is most naturally his hand.

decisions.choice: a double quotation mark opens here and closes at the end of verse 29; no inner quotation marks for each tribe
alternatives: single quotation marks around each tribe's saying
decisions.reason: The whole Blessing, verses 2-29, is one poem spoken by Moses. The short introductions ("Of Levi he said:") are part of the poem and its shape, not a change of speaker, so each tribe's saying is not set in quotation marks of its own; a colon follows the introduction. Words quoted inside the poem (verses 9 and 27) take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Moses said; for his people
decisions.reason: Readable names Moses as the speaker and says that "them" is God's people, as verses 3-5 show.

source.text: אַ֚ף חֹבֵ֣ב עַמִּ֔ים כָּל־קְדֹשָׁ֖יו בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְהֵם֙ תֻּכּ֣וּ לְרַגְלֶ֔ךָ יִשָּׂ֖א מִדַּבְּרֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also loving peoples; all his holy ones [are] in your hand; and they were led to your foot; he will take up from your words.

en.L: Indeed, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves [the] peoples; \q all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones [are] in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand; \q and they sit down at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet; \q [each] receives from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words.
en.B: Truly {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves the peoples; \q all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones are in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand. \q They sit down at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet, \q and each receives {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words.
en.R: He truly loves the tribes of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. \q All who are holy to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} are in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} care. \q They sit at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet \q and each one takes in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words.

decisions.choice: the peoples: the tribes of Israel, gathered as one people
decisions.reason: The plural can mean the nations, and some read the line as God's love for all peoples. But the verses around it speak of Israel, its holy ones and its tribes (verse 5), and Jacob was promised he would become "an assembly of peoples" (Genesis 28:3; 48:4). The line most likely speaks of the tribes.

decisions.choice: his holy ones ... your hand: both pronouns refer to God
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry often moves from speaking about God ("his") to speaking to him ("your") in one line (32:15-18). The holy ones are his people, set apart for him (7:6; 14:2), held safe in his hand.

decisions.choice: they sit down at your feet; each receives your words: the people gathered at Sinai to hear God's teaching
alternatives: they were led at your feet
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here. It probably means to sit or lie down, as learners sit at the feet of a teacher, or to follow close behind. The next words picture each one receiving God's words, as Israel did at Sinai (5:22-27). The exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: the tribes of his people; in your care
decisions.reason: Readable says which peoples are meant (see m1) and gives the sense of "in your hand".

source.text: תּוֹרָ֥ה צִוָּה־לָ֖נוּ מֹשֶׁ֑ה מוֹרָשָׁ֖ה קְהִלַּ֥ת יַעֲקֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: A law commanded to us Moses, a possession [of the] assembly of Jacob.

en.L: Moses commanded us a law, \q a possession for [the] assembly of Jacob.
en.B: Moses gave us a law to keep, \q the inheritance of the assembly of Jacob.
en.R: Moses gave us the teaching we must follow. \q It belongs to the assembly of Jacob's people as their own.

decisions.choice: us: the people speak in this line
decisions.reason: In the middle of Moses' blessing the people speak of "us" and of Moses by name. The line is a confession of the whole people, gathered as in verse 5. Some take it as a later voice; either way it is part of the poem.

decisions.choice: law: God's teaching as a whole, given through Moses
decisions.reason: As at 1:5, torah is more than a list of rules: it is everything God taught Israel through Moses.

decisions.choice: a possession: something handed down and kept as the people's own
decisions.reason: The word is used of the land given to Israel to own (Exodus 6:8). Here the law is the people's treasured inheritance.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for torah, as the terms for Deuteronomy set out.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י בִישֻׁר֖וּן מֶ֑לֶךְ בְּהִתְאַסֵּף֙ רָ֣אשֵׁי עָ֔ם יַ֖חַד שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he was in Jeshurun king, when gathered themselves [the] heads of [the] people, together [the] tribes of Israel.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became king in Jeshurun \q when [the] heads of [the] people gathered, \q the tribes of Israel together.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} became king in Jeshurun \q when the leaders of the people assembled, \q all the tribes of Israel together.
en.R: God became king over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel \q when their leaders came together \q with all the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: he became king: the LORD became Israel's king
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. In the poem the LORD is the one who comes and gives the law (verses 2-4), and the Song at the Sea ends with him reigning (Exodus 15:18). Some take the king to be Moses, the leader of the gathering, or read "there was a king" as a look ahead to Israel's kings. The kingship of the LORD fits the poem best, but the line does not say.

decisions.choice: Jeshurun: a name of honor for Israel
decisions.reason: The name probably comes from the word for "upright": Israel as the upright one God made it to be (32:15; 33:26; Isaiah 44:2).

decisions.choice: when the heads of the people gathered: the assembly at Sinai
decisions.reason: The leaders and tribes gathered before God at the mountain (4:10; 5:23), where the covenant made the LORD Israel's king.

decisions.choice: God became king over his people Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "Israel" for Jeshurun, as the terms for Deuteronomy set out, and names God as the king (see m1).

source.text: יְחִ֥י רְאוּבֵ֖ן וְאַל־יָמֹ֑ת וִיהִ֥י מְתָ֖יו מִסְפָּֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Let live Reuben and not let him die, and let be his men number.

en.L: Let Reuben live and not die, \q and let his men be [few in] number.
en.B: May Reuben live and not die out, \q even though his men are few.
en.R: May the tribe of Reuben live on and not die out, \q even though its people are few.

decisions.choice: and let his men be few in number: may Reuben survive, though small
alternatives: but let his men be few
and let not his men be few
decisions.reason: The words read "and let his men be a number", that is, few enough to count (Genesis 34:30). The line most likely asks that Reuben live on even though it is small. It could also be a wish that it stay small, as Reuben lost the firstborn's place (Genesis 49:3-4). Others carry the "not" of the first line into the second: "and let not his men be few". The Hebrew is short and the sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: Reuben: the firstborn's tribe, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Reuben was Jacob's firstborn, and his tribe settled east of the Jordan (3:12-16; Numbers 32). The prayer that it not die out suggests a tribe at risk.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Reuben; its people
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the name stands for the tribe, as in all these sayings.

source.text: וְזֹ֣את לִֽיהוּדָה֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ שְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ ק֣וֹל יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶל־עַמּ֖וֹ תְּבִיאֶ֑נּוּ יָדָיו֙ רָ֣ב ל֔וֹ וְעֵ֥זֶר מִצָּרָ֖יו תִּהְיֶֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And this for Judah, and he said: hear, Yahweh, [the] voice of Judah, and to his people you will bring him; his hands contended for him, and a help from his foes you will be.

en.L: And this [is] for Judah, and he said: \q Hear, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the voice of Judah, \q and bring him to his people; \q his hands contend for him, \q and a help against his foes may {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be.
en.B: This he said of Judah: \q Hear, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the voice of Judah, \q and bring him to his people. \q He fights for his cause with his own hands; \q be his help against his enemies.
en.R: This is what he said about Judah: \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, listen to Judah when they call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Bring them to their own people. \q They fight for themselves with all their strength. \q Help them against their enemies.

decisions.choice: hear the voice of Judah and bring him to his people: answer Judah's prayer in battle and bring him home
alternatives: bring him to his people: unite Judah with the rest of Israel
decisions.reason: Judah calls to God for help, most likely in war, and the prayer is that he come back safely to his people. Some see a prayer that Judah, when it stood apart from the other tribes, be joined to them again.

decisions.choice: his hands contend for him: Judah fights for his own cause
alternatives: let his hands be strong for him
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a statement, "with his hands he contends for it", or as a wish, "may his hands be enough for him". A change of one letter would give "your hands", God's hands, fighting for Judah. The line asks God to help where Judah's own strength is not enough.

decisions.choice: Simeon is not named
decisions.reason: Simeon has no saying of its own in the Blessing. Its land later lay inside Judah's (Joshua 19:1, 9), and Jacob had said Simeon would be scattered (Genesis 49:5-7).

decisions.choice: they; them; their
decisions.reason: Readable speaks of the tribe as "they", since the name stands for a whole people.

source.text: וּלְלֵוִ֣י אָמַ֔ר תֻּמֶּ֥יךָ וְאוּרֶ֖יךָ לְאִ֣ישׁ חֲסִידֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִסִּיתוֹ֙ בְּמַסָּ֔ה תְּרִיבֵ֖הוּ עַל־מֵ֥י מְרִיבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And for Levi he said: your Thummim and your Urim [are] for [the] man of your faithful one, whom you tested at Massah; you contended [with] him at [the] waters of Meribah.

en.L: And of Levi he said: \q Your Thummim and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Urim [belong] to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful man, \q whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} tested at Massah, \q with whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} contended at the waters of Meribah,
en.B: Of Levi he said: \q Your Thummim and Urim belong to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful one, \q the man {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} tested at Massah, \q with whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} strove at the waters of Meribah,
en.R: This is what he said about Levi: \q Your Thummim and Urim, used to learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will, \q belong to the men who are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You tested them at Massah and argued with them at the waters of Meribah.

decisions.choice: Thummim and Urim: the lots the high priest used to ask God's will
decisions.reason: They were kept in the breastpiece of the high priest (Exodus 28:30; Leviticus 8:8) and used to receive God's answer to a question (Numbers 27:21; 1 Samuel 14:41). Only here is Thummim named first. They belong to Levi because the priests came from that tribe.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew begins "your Thummim"
decisions.reason: The Greek translation, and a Hebrew text of these verses found at Qumran, begin "Give to Levi your Thummim", making the line a prayer. The source text has only "of Levi he said". Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: Massah and Meribah: where Israel tested God, and Levi was tested
decisions.reason: At Massah and Meribah the people tested the LORD and quarreled with Moses (Exodus 17:1-7; Numbers 20:1-13; 6:16). Here it is God who tests Levi there; Moses and Aaron, both of Levi, stood at the center of those events. The tribe was proved in the hard times of the wilderness.

decisions.choice: your faithful man: Levi, the one loyal to God
decisions.reason: The word means one who is loyal and devoted, from the word for steadfast love. It speaks of the tribe as one man, as the next verse does.

decisions.choice: used to learn your will; them
alternatives: your Thummim and your Urim; him
decisions.reason: Readable says briefly what Thummim and Urim were for, and speaks of the tribe's men in the plural.

source.text: הָאֹמֵ֞ר לְאָבִ֤יו וּלְאִמּוֹ֙ לֹ֣א רְאִיתִ֔יו וְאֶת־אֶחָיו֙ לֹ֣א הִכִּ֔יר וְאֶת־בָּנָ֖יו לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע כִּ֤י שָֽׁמְרוּ֙ אִמְרָתֶ֔ךָ וּבְרִֽיתְךָ֖ יִנְצֹֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: The [one] saying of his father and of his mother, I have not seen him; and his brothers he did not recognize, and his sons he did not know; for they kept your word, and your covenant they guarded.

en.L: who said of his father and of his mother, 'I have not seen him'; \q and his brothers he did not acknowledge, \q and his children he did not know; \q for they kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant they guarded.
en.B: who said of his father and mother, 'I have no regard for them.' \q He would not acknowledge his brothers \q or claim his own children, \q for they kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word \q and guarded {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant.
en.R: They said about their father and mother, 'They mean nothing to us.' \q They turned away from their brothers \q and did not favor their own children. \q They obeyed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word \q and kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} covenant.

decisions.choice: father, mother, brothers, children: the Levites' loyalty at the golden calf
decisions.reason: When Israel made the golden calf, the Levites rallied to Moses and struck down the guilty, sparing no brother, friend or neighbor (Exodus 32:26-29). Phinehas showed the same zeal (Numbers 25:7-13). Loyalty to the LORD came before loyalty to family (13:7-12).

decisions.choice: I have not seen him; did not acknowledge; did not know: did not take the side of family
decisions.reason: Not seeing, not recognizing and not knowing are ways of saying he refused to favor his own kin when they stood against God. The words do not mean he never knew them.

decisions.choice: he ... they: the tribe spoken of as one man and as many
decisions.reason: The verse moves from "he" to "they", the tribe as a single figure and as its members, as Hebrew often does.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: Words quoted inside the Blessing take single quotation marks, since the whole poem is inside the double quotation mark that opened at verse 2.

decisions.choice: They mean nothing to us; they
alternatives: I have not seen him; he
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the saying and keeps the tribe in the plural, as in verse 8.

source.text: יוֹר֤וּ מִשְׁפָּטֶ֨יךָ֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וְתוֹרָתְךָ֖ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יָשִׂ֤ימוּ קְטוֹרָה֙ בְּאַפֶּ֔ךָ וְכָלִ֖יל עַֽל־מִזְבְּחֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: They will teach your judgments to Jacob, and your law to Israel; they will put incense in your nose, and whole offering on your altar.

en.L: They teach {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments to Jacob \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law to Israel; \q they put incense in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} nostrils \q and whole offerings on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar.
en.B: They teach {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings to Jacob \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} law to Israel; \q they set incense before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} \q and whole burnt offerings on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar.
en.R: They teach {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rules to Jacob's people \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching to Israel. \q They burn incense for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to smell \q and offer whole burnt offerings on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar.

decisions.choice: they teach: the priests' task of teaching God's law
decisions.reason: The priests taught Israel the LORD's rulings and decided hard cases by them (17:9-11; 24:8; Leviticus 10:11; Malachi 2:6-7). Teaching comes first here, before the offerings.

decisions.choice: in your nostrils: before you, for you to smell
decisions.reason: The smoke of incense rising to God is spoken of as something he smells and delights in (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 1:9).

decisions.choice: whole offering: an offering burned completely on the altar
decisions.reason: The word means "complete, whole". It names a burnt offering of which nothing was kept back (Leviticus 6:15-16; 1 Samuel 7:9).

decisions.choice: rulings; rules; teaching
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the settled words for mishpatim and torah: Literal "judgments" and "law", Balanced "rulings" and "law", Readable "rules" and "teaching".

decisions.choice: before you
decisions.reason: Balanced says where the incense is offered rather than keep the picture of God smelling it; Readable keeps the picture.

source.text: בָּרֵ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ חֵיל֔וֹ וּפֹ֥עַל יָדָ֖יו תִּרְצֶ֑ה מְחַ֨ץ מָתְנַ֧יִם קָמָ֛יו וּמְשַׂנְאָ֖יו מִן־יְקוּמֽוּן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Bless, Yahweh, his strength, and [the] work of his hands may you accept; smite [the] loins of those rising against him and those hating him from their rising.

en.L: Bless, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, his strength, \q and the work of his hands may {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} accept; \q strike the loins of those who rise against him and of those who hate him, so that they do not rise.
en.B: Bless his strength, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and be pleased with the work of his hands. \q Crush the loins of all who rise against him and of those who hate him, so that they never rise again.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, bless the strength of Levi's tribe, \q and accept the work they do for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Crush their enemies and those who hate them so that they never get up again.

decisions.choice: his strength: his ability and power
decisions.reason: The word can mean strength, ability or wealth. The Levites had no land of their own (10:9; 18:1-2), so the prayer is most likely for their strength in God's service.

decisions.choice: strike the loins: break their strength
decisions.reason: The loins are the hips and lower back, the seat of a man's strength (Psalm 69:24; Nahum 2:2). A blow there leaves an enemy unable to stand.

decisions.choice: those who rise against him: those who challenge Levi's priesthood
decisions.reason: The rebellion of Korah, Dathan and Abiram was a challenge to the tribe chosen to serve (Numbers 16-17). The prayer asks God to defend those he has chosen.

decisions.choice: the work they do for you
decisions.reason: Readable says that the work is the priests' service to God.

source.text: לְבִנְיָמִ֣ן אָמַ֔ר יְדִ֣יד יְהֹוָ֔ה יִשְׁכֹּ֥ן לָבֶ֖טַח עָלָ֑יו חֹפֵ֤ף עָלָיו֙ כָּל־הַיּ֔וֹם וּבֵ֥ין כְּתֵיפָ֖יו שָׁכֵֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For Benjamin he said: [the] beloved of Yahweh will dwell in security upon him; covering over him all the day, and between his shoulders he dwells.

en.L: Of Benjamin he said: \q [The] beloved of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dwells in safety beside {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shields him all the day, \q and between {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} shoulders he dwells.
en.B: Of Benjamin he said: \q The one {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves lives in safety beside {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shelters him all day long, \q and Benjamin rests between {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} shoulders.
en.R: This is what he said about Benjamin: \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} loves Benjamin, who lives safely beside {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q He protects Benjamin all day long, \q and Benjamin rests between {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} shoulders, carried by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the beloved of the LORD: Benjamin, loved by God
decisions.reason: Benjamin was Jacob's youngest son, the one his father loved and would not let go (Genesis 35:18; 44:20). The same word is used for those God loves (Psalm 127:2; Jeremiah 11:15). It may also look ahead to Solomon, named Jedidiah, "beloved of the LORD" (2 Samuel 12:25).

decisions.choice: between his shoulders he dwells: Benjamin rests between God's shoulders, carried as a child is carried
alternatives: the LORD dwells between Benjamin's shoulders, among his hills
decisions.reason: The verse does not name who rests and whose shoulders are meant. The first lines speak of God sheltering Benjamin, so the last most likely pictures God carrying him on his back, as a father carries his son (1:31). It may instead mean that the LORD dwells between Benjamin's "shoulders", the slopes of his hill country, since the word is used for the side of a hill (Joshua 15:8) and the temple in Jerusalem stood on Benjamin's border (Joshua 18:16). Either way, Benjamin lives close to God.

decisions.choice: beside him ... he shields him: the Hebrew has "upon him" twice
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "upon him" at the end of the first line and "over him" in the second. Some think the first was copied by mistake for a title of God, "the Most High", which has similar letters. The Greek translation reads "God shades him". The source text is kept, and "upon him" is taken to mean close beside the LORD. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: Benjamin rests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Benjamin as the one who rests, following the reading in m2.

decisions.choice: carried by him
decisions.reason: Readable says what resting between his shoulders means on the reading of m2.

source.text: וּלְיוֹסֵ֣ף אָמַ֔ר מְבֹרֶ֥כֶת יְהֹוָ֖ה אַרְצ֑וֹ מִמֶּ֤גֶד שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ מִטָּ֔ל וּמִתְּה֖וֹם רֹבֶ֥צֶת תָּֽחַת׃

records.literal_gloss: And for Joseph he said: blessed of Yahweh [is] his land, from [the] choicest of heavens, from dew, and from [the] deep lying beneath,

en.L: And of Joseph he said: \q Blessed by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [be] his land, \q with the choicest gifts of heaven, with the dew, \q and with the deep that lies beneath,
en.B: Of Joseph he said: \q Blessed by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be his land \q with the finest gifts of the sky, with dew, \q and with the deep waters that lie below,
en.R: This is what he said about Joseph: \q May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless his land \q with the best gifts from the sky, the dew, \q and with water from deep under the ground.

decisions.choice: heaven and the deep that lies beneath: Jacob's blessing of Joseph
decisions.reason: Jacob blessed Joseph with "blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies beneath" (Genesis 49:25-26), and verses 13-16 take up the same words. The deep is the water under the earth that feeds springs and wells (8:7). The word for "lies" is used of an animal lying down (Genesis 49:9).

decisions.choice: choicest gifts: the best and most precious things
decisions.reason: The word, used five times in verses 13-16, means what is excellent and rare. It is used of the fine gifts given to Rebekah (Genesis 24:53) and of choice fruit (Song 4:13).

decisions.choice: with the dew
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "with dew". A small change in one letter would give "from above", making the line "the choicest gifts of heaven above", as in Genesis 49:25. The source text is kept: dew is the gift of the sky that waters the land in the dry season (32:2; 33:28).

decisions.choice: the deep waters
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the deep is.

source.text: וּמִמֶּ֖גֶד תְּבוּאֹ֣ת שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וּמִמֶּ֖גֶד גֶּ֥רֶשׁ יְרָחִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and from [the] choicest of [the] produce of [the] sun, and from [the] choicest of [the] yield of [the] months,

en.L: and with the choicest produce of the sun, \q and with the choicest yield of the months,
en.B: with the best that the sun brings forth \q and the richest crops of every month,
en.R: May it have the best crops that the sun ripens \q and the best harvest of every month.

decisions.choice: the produce of the sun and the yield of the months: the crops that ripen through the year
decisions.reason: The sun and the months (the word is related to "moon") are paired. Fruit ripens in the sun, and each month brings its own harvest. The word for yield is rare and means what is pushed out, as plants put forth growth.

decisions.choice: May it have
decisions.reason: Readable makes each verse a sentence of its own; "it" is Joseph's land.

source.text: וּמֵרֹ֖אשׁ הַרְרֵי־קֶ֑דֶם וּמִמֶּ֖גֶד גִּבְע֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and from [the] top of [the] mountains of ancient time, and from [the] choicest of [the] hills of antiquity,

en.L: and with the best of the ancient mountains, \q and with the choicest gifts of the everlasting hills,
en.B: with the finest yield of the ancient mountains \q and the choicest gifts of the everlasting hills,
en.R: May the old mountains give it their best \q and the hills that last forever give their finest gifts.

decisions.choice: the best: the finest produce
decisions.reason: The word is "head", which can mean the top of a mountain or the first and best of something. Paired with "choicest gifts", it means the finest produce of the hills.

decisions.choice: the ancient mountains and everlasting hills: Jacob's blessing of Joseph
decisions.reason: The same pair of words is in Genesis 49:26. The hills are called ancient because they have stood since creation; Joseph's tribes would hold the hill country of central Canaan.

source.text: וּמִמֶּ֗גֶד אֶ֚רֶץ וּמְלֹאָ֔הּ וּרְצ֥וֹן שֹׁכְנִ֖י סְנֶ֑ה תָּב֨וֹאתָה֙ לְרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹסֵ֔ף וּלְקָדְקֹ֖ד נְזִ֥יר אֶחָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: and from [the] choicest of [the] earth and its fullness, and [the] favor of [the] one dwelling [in the] bush; let it come to [the] head of Joseph, and to [the] crown of [the] head of [the] one set apart [among] his brothers.

en.L: and with the choicest gifts of the earth and its fullness, \q and the favor of the one who dwelt in the bush. \q Let it come on the head of Joseph, \q and on the crown of the head of the one set apart among his brothers.
en.B: with the best gifts of the earth and all that fills it, \q and the favor of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who dwelt in the bush. \q May all this rest on the head of Joseph, \q on the brow of the one set apart from his brothers.
en.R: May his land have the best gifts of the earth and all that grows on it, \q and the kindness of God, who was present in the burning bush. \q May all these blessings come to Joseph, \q to the head of the one who was set apart from his brothers.

decisions.choice: the one who dwelt in the bush: God, who spoke to Moses from the burning bush
decisions.reason: The word for bush is used only in the story of the burning bush (Exodus 3:2-4). The God who appeared to Moses there is the one whose favor rests on Joseph. The word sounds like Sinai (verse 2).

decisions.choice: the one set apart among his brothers: Joseph, separated from his brothers and raised above them
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a Nazirite, someone set apart, and the whole line repeats Genesis 49:26. Joseph was parted from his brothers when they sold him and was raised to rule over Egypt and over them (Genesis 37:28; 42:6). The sense here is a person singled out, not a Nazirite's vow.

decisions.choice: let it come: the blessing as a whole
decisions.reason: The verb is singular: all the gifts of verses 13-16 are spoken of as one blessing that comes to rest on Joseph's head, as a hand is laid on the head in blessing (Genesis 48:14).

decisions.choice: God, who was present in the burning bush
alternatives: the one who dwelt in the bush
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says which bush is meant.

source.text: בְּכ֨וֹר שׁוֹר֜וֹ הָדָ֣ר ל֗וֹ וְקַרְנֵ֤י רְאֵם֙ קַרְנָ֔יו בָּהֶ֗ם עַמִּ֛ים יְנַגַּ֥ח יַחְדָּ֖ו אַפְסֵי־אָ֑רֶץ וְהֵם֙ רִבְב֣וֹת אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְהֵ֖ם אַלְפֵ֥י מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] firstborn of his bull, majesty [is] to him, and horns of [a] wild ox [are] his horns; with them peoples he will gore together, [the] ends of [the] earth; and they [are the] ten thousands of Ephraim, and they [are the] thousands of Manasseh.

en.L: His firstborn bull, majesty [is] his, and his horns [are the] horns of a wild ox; \q with them he gores [the] peoples, all together, [to the] ends of the earth; \q and they [are] the ten thousands of Ephraim, \q and they [are] the thousands of Manasseh.
en.B: In majesty he is like a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a wild ox. \q With them he gores the peoples, all of them, to the ends of the earth. \q Such are the ten thousands of Ephraim, \q such are the thousands of Manasseh.
en.R: Joseph is like a firstborn bull, splendid and strong, with horns like a wild ox. \q With them he will push back nations as far as the ends of the earth. \q These horns are the tens of thousands of Ephraim's people \q and the thousands of Manasseh's people.

decisions.choice: his firstborn bull: Joseph, given the firstborn's place, pictured as a young bull
decisions.reason: Joseph received the firstborn's double share through his two sons (Genesis 48:5; 1 Chronicles 5:1-2), and a bull is a picture of strength. "His" may refer to Jacob, whose firstborn Joseph became, or to Joseph, whose firstborn by blessing was Ephraim (Genesis 48:19-20). The Greek translation has "a firstborn bull", without "his". Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: wild ox: a large, strong wild bull
decisions.reason: The word names the wild ox, an animal of great strength that cannot be tamed (Numbers 23:22; Job 39:9-10). It is a real animal, now extinct, not a one-horned creature of legend.

decisions.choice: ten thousands of Ephraim, thousands of Manasseh: the younger son set above the elder
decisions.reason: Jacob put Ephraim, the younger, ahead of Manasseh (Genesis 48:19-20), and the larger number goes to Ephraim. The two horns of the bull stand for the two tribes. The numbers are a way of saying "very many", not a count.

decisions.choice: like a firstborn bull
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the picture into a comparison so that it is clear Joseph is the bull.

decisions.choice: wild ox
decisions.reason: Older English Bibles, following the Greek and Latin translations, said "unicorn". "Wild ox" names the real animal (see m2).

decisions.choice: push back
decisions.reason: Readable says what goring with the horns means for a tribe in war, and says who "they" are.

source.text: וְלִזְבוּלֻ֣ן אָמַ֔ר שְׂמַ֥ח זְבוּלֻ֖ן בְּצֵאתֶ֑ךָ וְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר בְּאֹהָלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And for Zebulun he said: rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.

en.L: And of Zebulun he said: \q Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, \q and Issachar, in your tents.
en.B: Of Zebulun he said: \q Rejoice, Zebulun, when you go out, \q and you, Issachar, in your tents.
en.R: This is what he said about Zebulun: \q Be glad, Zebulun, when you go out to trade, \q and you, Issachar, when you stay at home in your tents.

decisions.choice: your going out ... your tents: at work abroad and at home
decisions.reason: Going out and staying in the tent is a pair for the whole of life, away and at home. Zebulun was to live by the sea and its trade (Genesis 49:13), and Issachar to settle on its land (Genesis 49:14-15). Both are told to rejoice.

decisions.choice: Issachar under Zebulun's heading
decisions.reason: The two tribes, both sons of Leah born one after the other (Genesis 30:17-20), share one saying here and lived side by side in the north.

decisions.choice: to trade; when you stay at home
alternatives: in your going out; in your tents
decisions.reason: Readable says what going out and the tents stand for (see m1).

source.text: עַמִּים֙ הַר־יִקְרָ֔אוּ שָׁ֖ם יִזְבְּח֣וּ זִבְחֵי־צֶ֑דֶק כִּ֣י שֶׁ֤פַע יַמִּים֙ יִינָ֔קוּ וּשְׂפוּנֵ֖י טְמ֥וּנֵי חֽוֹל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Peoples [to the] mountain they will call; there they will sacrifice sacrifices of righteousness; for [the] abundance of [the] seas they will suck, and hidden [things] of hidden [things] of sand.

en.L: They will call peoples [to the] mountain; \q there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness; \q for they will suck the abundance of the seas \q and the hidden treasures of the sand.
en.B: They will call peoples to the mountain, \q and there they will offer right sacrifices; \q for they will draw from the wealth of the seas \q and the treasures hidden in the sand.
en.R: They will invite other peoples to the mountain \q to offer the right sacrifices there. \q They will grow rich from the sea \q and from treasures hidden in the sand.

decisions.choice: they will call peoples to the mountain: they will invite others to worship with them
alternatives: the peoples will call to the mountain
decisions.reason: The mountain is not named. It may be Mount Tabor, which stood where the lands of Zebulun and Issachar met (Joshua 19:12, 22), or the mountain where God would be worshiped (Exodus 15:17). The peoples may be other tribes or foreigners met in trade. The sense of the line is not certain.

decisions.choice: sacrifices of righteousness: sacrifices offered rightly, as God requires
decisions.reason: The phrase means sacrifices that are right and acceptable, offered in the right way and with the right heart (Psalm 4:6; 51:21).

decisions.choice: they will suck the abundance of the seas: they will grow rich from the sea
decisions.reason: To suck is to draw nourishment, as a child at the breast (32:13; Isaiah 60:16). The hidden treasures of the sand may be goods from sea trade, the shellfish that gave purple dye, or the sand from which glass was made; the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: draw from; grow rich from
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture of sucking means; Literal keeps it.

source.text: וּלְגָ֣ד אָמַ֔ר בָּר֖וּךְ מַרְחִ֣יב גָּ֑ד כְּלָבִ֣יא שָׁכֵ֔ן וְטָרַ֥ף זְר֖וֹעַ אַף־קָדְקֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And for Gad he said: blessed [is the one] enlarging Gad; like a lion he dwells, and he tears [the] arm, also [the] crown of [the] head.

en.L: And of Gad he said: \q Blessed [be the one] who enlarges Gad; \q like a lion he dwells, \q and he tears the arm, yes, the crown of the head.
en.B: Of Gad he said: \q Blessed is the one who gives Gad room to grow! \q He lies down like a lion \q and tears off arm and scalp.
en.R: This is what he said about Gad: \q Praise God, who gives Gad more land! \q Gad lives like a lion \q that tears at the arm and the head of its prey.

decisions.choice: blessed be the one who enlarges Gad: praise to God, who gives Gad wide land
decisions.reason: The one who enlarges is God, who gives room and land (Genesis 26:22; 12:20). Gad received broad pasture lands east of the Jordan (3:12-16; Numbers 32:1-5). The name Gad sounds like a word for raiding bands (Genesis 49:19).

decisions.choice: like a lion he dwells and tears: Gad as a fierce warrior
decisions.reason: The word may mean a lion or a lioness. The lion lies at rest in its den and tears its prey, arm and head. Gad's fighting men were known for strength (1 Chronicles 12:9).

decisions.choice: Praise God, who gives Gad more land
alternatives: Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one praised (see m1) and says what "enlarges" means.

source.text: וַיַּ֤רְא רֵאשִׁית֙ ל֔וֹ כִּי־שָׁ֛ם חֶלְקַ֥ת מְחֹקֵ֖ק סָפ֑וּן וַיֵּתֵא֙ רָ֣אשֵׁי עָ֔ם צִדְקַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֖יו עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he saw [the] first for himself, for there [the] portion of [a] commander [was] reserved; and he came [with the] heads of [the] people; [the] righteousness of Yahweh he did, and his judgments with Israel.

en.L: And he chose the first [part] for himself, \q for there a commander's portion was reserved; \q and he came [with] the heads of the people; \q he carried out the righteousness of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments with Israel.
en.B: He chose the best land for himself, \q for a commander's share was kept for him there. \q He marched with the leaders of the people; \q he carried out the justice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings together with Israel.
en.R: Gad took the best land for itself, \q the share kept for a leader. \q Gad marched with the leaders of the people. \q It did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right \q and obeyed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rules with the rest of Israel.

decisions.choice: he chose the first part for himself: Gad asked for its land first
decisions.reason: "Saw for himself" means to pick out, choose (Genesis 22:8; 1 Samuel 16:1). Gad, with Reuben, asked Moses for the land east of the Jordan before the conquest of Canaan began (3:12-16; Numbers 32:1-5).

decisions.choice: a commander's portion was reserved: a share fit for a leader was kept for him
alternatives: the lawgiver's portion was hidden there
the portion assigned by the leader
decisions.reason: The word means one who gives orders or decrees: a ruler, commander or lawgiver. The line may mean that Gad's land was the share of a leading tribe, or the share a leader (Moses) assigned it. An old Jewish reading takes it as the place where Moses, the lawgiver, was hidden in his grave (34:6). The word for "reserved" can also mean "hidden". The sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: he came with the heads of the people: Gad went at the front of Israel's army
alternatives: the heads of the people came
the heads of the people gathered
decisions.reason: Gad promised to cross the Jordan armed, ahead of the other tribes, and fight until the land was taken (3:18-20; Numbers 32:20-22; Joshua 4:12). The line most likely refers to that. It can also be read "when the heads of the people came" or, with a small change, "gathered", as in verse 5.

decisions.choice: the righteousness of the LORD and his judgments: what the LORD rightly required
decisions.reason: Gad did what the LORD had said was right and kept the terms he had set, by keeping its promise (Numbers 32:31). "With Israel" means together with the other tribes.

decisions.choice: justice
decisions.reason: Balanced says "justice" for the LORD's right requirements carried out; Literal keeps "righteousness".

decisions.choice: Gad; it
decisions.reason: Readable names Gad and speaks of the tribe as "it".

source.text: וּלְדָ֣ן אָמַ֔ר דָּ֖ן גּ֣וּר אַרְיֵ֑ה יְזַנֵּ֖ק מִן־הַבָּשָֽׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: And for Dan he said: Dan [is] a cub of a lion; he will leap from the Bashan.

en.L: And of Dan he said: \q Dan [is] a lion's cub; \q he leaps out from Bashan.
en.B: Of Dan he said: \q Dan is a lion's cub \q that springs out from Bashan.
en.R: This is what he said about Dan: \q Dan is like a young lion \q that leaps out from Bashan.

decisions.choice: leaps out: springs forward suddenly
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here. It most likely means to leap or spring, as a young lion springs from cover on its prey.

decisions.choice: Bashan: the high, wooded country east of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Bashan, taken from Og (3:1-11), was known for its forests and wild animals. Dan first received land near the coast (Joshua 19:40-46) but later moved to the far north, close to Bashan (Judges 18:27-29). The young lion is a picture of a small tribe that strikes with sudden force.

decisions.choice: a lion's cub: the picture Jacob used for Judah
decisions.reason: Jacob called Judah "a lion's cub" (Genesis 49:9); here Moses uses it of Dan. Jacob had pictured Dan as a snake by the road (Genesis 49:17).

decisions.choice: like a young lion
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison and says "young lion" for a cub that is old enough to hunt.

source.text: וּלְנַפְתָּלִ֣י אָמַ֔ר נַפְתָּלִי֙ שְׂבַ֣ע רָצ֔וֹן וּמָלֵ֖א בִּרְכַּ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה יָ֥ם וְדָר֖וֹם יְרָֽשָׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And for Naphtali he said: Naphtali, satisfied [with] favor, and full [of the] blessing of Yahweh, west and south take possession.

en.L: And of Naphtali he said: \q Naphtali, satisfied [with] favor, \q and full of the blessing of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q take possession of [the] sea and [the] south.
en.B: Of Naphtali he said: \q Naphtali, rich in favor \q and full of the blessing of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q take possession of the lake and the south.
en.R: This is what he said about Naphtali: \q Naphtali, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been very good to you \q and filled you with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blessing. \q Take the land by the lake and to the south.

decisions.choice: satisfied with favor: having all of God's goodwill one could want
decisions.reason: To be satisfied is to have had one's fill. The favor is the LORD's, as the parallel line shows, and as in verse 16.

decisions.choice: the sea and the south: the Sea of Galilee and the land south of Naphtali's hills
decisions.reason: The word for sea also means "west", the direction of the Mediterranean. Naphtali's land lay west of the Sea of Galilee and ran down beside it (Joshua 19:32-39), so the lake is most likely meant. The south may be the warm, fertile land at the lake's southern end.

decisions.choice: the LORD has been very good to you and filled you with his blessing
alternatives: satisfied with favor and full of the blessing of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable turns the two descriptions into a sentence about what the LORD has done for Naphtali.

decisions.choice: the lake
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "lake" for the Sea of Galilee, a body of fresh water (see m2).

source.text: וּלְאָשֵׁ֣ר אָמַ֔ר בָּר֥וּךְ מִבָּנִ֖ים אָשֵׁ֑ר יְהִ֤י רְצוּי֙ אֶחָ֔יו וְטֹבֵ֥ל בַּשֶּׁ֖מֶן רַגְלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And for Asher he said: blessed above sons [is] Asher; let him be favored [by] his brothers, and dipping in oil his foot.

en.L: And of Asher he said: \q Blessed above [the] sons [be] Asher; \q let him be the favored one of his brothers, \q and let him dip his foot in oil.
en.B: Of Asher he said: \q Most blessed of the sons is Asher; \q may he be the favorite of his brothers \q and dip his feet in oil.
en.R: This is what he said about Asher: \q Asher is the most blessed of the sons. \q May his brothers love him, \q and may he have so much olive oil that he could wash his feet in it.

decisions.choice: blessed above the sons: the most blessed of Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: The words can mean "blessed more than the other sons" or "blessed with many sons". The name Asher means "happy" or "blessed" (Genesis 30:13), and the next line, on his brothers, suggests a comparison with them.

decisions.choice: dip his foot in oil: have olive oil in plenty
decisions.reason: Asher's land in the hills of western Galilee was rich in olive trees (Genesis 49:20). Oil so plentiful that one could wash one's feet in it is a picture of wealth (Job 29:6).

decisions.choice: so much olive oil that he could wash his feet in it
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (see m2).

source.text: בַּרְזֶ֥ל וּנְחֹ֖שֶׁת מִנְעָלֶ֑יךָ וּכְיָמֶ֖יךָ דָּבְאֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Iron and bronze [are] your bolts, and as your days your strength.

en.L: Iron and bronze [be] your bolts, \q and as your days, [so] your strength.
en.B: Your bolts will be iron and bronze, \q and your strength will last as long as your days.
en.R: Your gates will be locked with bars of iron and bronze, \q and you will be strong as long as you live.

decisions.choice: bolts: the bars that lock a city's gates
decisions.reason: The word is used of the bars of gates (Nehemiah 3:3, 6). Iron and bronze bolts mean strong, safe towns. A word spelled almost the same way means a sandal, and some read "your sandals will be iron and bronze", sure footing for a mountain tribe.

decisions.choice: your strength: the strength that keeps you safe
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. The context, with iron and bronze, suggests strength, lasting all your life. It may instead mean rest or security. The sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: your: Asher, addressed directly
decisions.reason: The blessing of Asher turns to speak to the tribe. Some take this verse as a closing word to all the tribes, but it follows straight on from verse 24.

decisions.choice: Your gates will be locked with bars
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bolts are for.

source.text: אֵ֥ין כָּאֵ֖ל יְשֻׁר֑וּן רֹכֵ֤ב שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ בְעֶזְרֶ֔ךָ וּבְגַאֲוָת֖וֹ שְׁחָקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: There is none like God, Jeshurun, riding [the] heavens to your help, and in his majesty [the] clouds.

en.L: There is none like God, Jeshurun, \q riding the heavens to your help, \q and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majesty the clouds.
en.B: There is no one like God, Jeshurun, \q who rides through the heavens to help you \q and through the skies in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majesty.
en.R: Israel, there is no one like God. \q He rides across the sky to help you; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rides on the clouds in majesty.

decisions.choice: like God, Jeshurun: Jeshurun is addressed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels make Jeshurun the one spoken to: "there is none like God, Jeshurun". The same letters with other vowels read "there is none like the God of Jeshurun", and the Greek translation has "like the God of the beloved one". The meaning is much the same. On Jeshurun, see verse 5.

decisions.choice: riding the heavens and the clouds: the LORD comes as king and warrior from the sky
decisions.reason: The picture of God riding the heavens or the clouds to help his people is found in the Psalms (Psalm 68:5, 34; 104:3; Isaiah 19:1). In old Canaanite poems the storm god Baal was called "rider of the clouds"; here the title belongs to Israel's God alone. The poem now returns to praise God, as it began in verses 2-5.

decisions.choice: Israel
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, Readable says "Israel" for Jeshurun.

source.text: מְעֹנָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵי קֶ֔דֶם וּמִתַּ֖חַת זְרֹעֹ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם וַיְגָ֧רֶשׁ מִפָּנֶ֛יךָ אוֹיֵ֖ב וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַשְׁמֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] dwelling place [is the] God of ancient time, and from beneath [are the] arms of eternity; and he drove out from before you [the] enemy, and he said, Destroy!

en.L: [A] dwelling place [is the] God of old, \q and underneath [are the] everlasting arms; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drove out the enemy before you and said, 'Destroy!'
en.B: The God of old is a refuge, \q and underneath are arms that last forever. \q He drove out the enemy before you and said, 'Destroy them!'
en.R: The God who has always lived is your safe home, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms that last forever hold you up. \q He drove out your enemies ahead of you and told you, 'Destroy them!'

decisions.choice: the God of old is a dwelling place: the eternal God is the home and refuge of his people
alternatives: the God of old is a refuge
decisions.reason: The word means a den or dwelling, a place to live and to hide in safety (Psalm 90:1; 91:9, where God is the dwelling place of his people). "Of old" means from the beginning, before all things.

decisions.choice: underneath are the everlasting arms: God's arms hold his people up
alternatives: (he subdues) the arms of the ancient ones
under him are the arms of the world
decisions.reason: The line is short and its grammar is hard. Most simply it pictures God's arms, which never tire, holding his people from beneath (1:31; Isaiah 46:3-4). Some read the same letters differently, or with small changes, as "he humbles the gods of old and breaks the strength of the ancient ones", which would lead into the driving out of the enemy. The source text supports the first reading, but it is not certain.

decisions.choice: he drove out the enemy and said, Destroy: the conquest of the land
decisions.reason: God drives out the nations before Israel and commands Israel to destroy them (7:1-2; 9:3; Exodus 23:31). The poem speaks of the conquest as already done, so certain is God's promise.

decisions.choice: Destroy them!
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the command an object, as English needs. Literal keeps the bare command. It is set in single quotation marks inside the Blessing (see verse 9).

decisions.choice: your safe home; his arms that last forever hold you up
alternatives: a dwelling place; underneath are the everlasting arms
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (see m1 and m2).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכֹּן֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל בֶּ֤טַח בָּדָד֙ עֵ֣ין יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ דָּגָ֣ן וְתִיר֑וֹשׁ אַף־שָׁמָ֖יו יַֽעַרְפוּטָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt Israel [in] security, alone [the] spring of Jacob, to a land of grain and new wine; also his heavens drip dew.

en.L: So Israel dwells in safety, the spring of Jacob alone, \q in a land of grain and new wine; \q even his heavens drip dew.
en.B: So Israel lives in safety, Jacob's spring secure by itself, \q in a land of grain and new wine, \q where his skies drop dew.
en.R: So Israel lives safely, Jacob's people by themselves, \q in a land of grain and new wine, \q where the sky drops dew.

decisions.choice: the spring of Jacob alone: Jacob's descendants living apart, untroubled
decisions.reason: The spring is a picture of Jacob's descendants, flowing from him as water from a source (Psalm 68:27; Isaiah 48:1). "Alone" means living apart in safety, with no enemy to fear (Numbers 23:9; Jeremiah 49:31). With a small change one word would be a verb, "Jacob dwells alone", which gives the same sense.

decisions.choice: his heavens: the sky over Jacob's land
decisions.reason: "His" most likely refers to Jacob, whose land is watered by the dew of its sky (Genesis 27:28). It could refer to God, who gives the dew.

decisions.choice: Jacob's people by themselves; the sky
alternatives: the spring of Jacob alone; his heavens
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the spring stands for (see m1) and does not repeat the pronoun.

source.text: אַשְׁרֶ֨יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל מִ֣י כָמ֗וֹךָ עַ֚ם נוֹשַׁ֣ע בַּֽיהוָ֔ה מָגֵ֣ן עֶזְרֶ֔ךָ וַאֲשֶׁר־חֶ֖רֶב גַּאֲוָתֶ֑ךָ וְיִכָּֽחֲשׁ֤וּ אֹיְבֶ֨יךָ֙ לָ֔ךְ וְאַתָּ֖ה עַל־בָּמוֹתֵ֥ימוֹ תִדְרֹֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Happy [are] you, Israel! Who [is] like you, a people saved by Yahweh, [the] shield of your help, and who [is the] sword of your majesty! And will cringe your enemies to you, and you on their high places will tread.

en.L: Happy [are] you, Israel! Who [is] like you, a people saved by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the shield of your help, \q and who [is] the sword of your majesty! \q And your enemies will cringe before you, \q and you will tread on their high places."
en.B: How happy you are, Israel! Who is like you, a people {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has saved? \q He is the shield that helps you \q and the sword that brings you triumph. \q Your enemies will come cringing to you, \q and you will tread upon their heights."
en.R: Israel, how happy you are! No other people is like you, saved by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q He is the shield that protects you \q and the sword that wins your victories. \q Your enemies will bow before you in fear, \q and you will march over their high hills."

decisions.choice: happy: in a state of blessing, well off
decisions.reason: The word describes the good state of one God has blessed (Psalm 1:1; 33:12, "happy the nation whose God is the LORD"). It is a different word from the "blessed" of the tribes' sayings.

decisions.choice: the shield of your help and the sword of your majesty: the LORD himself defends Israel and wins its battles
decisions.reason: The LORD is both the shield that guards Israel and the sword that gives it victory (Genesis 15:1; Psalm 33:20). Israel's glory is not its own strength but the God who saves it.

decisions.choice: your enemies will cringe before you: they will come to you in fear, yielding
decisions.reason: The verb means to come cringing, to submit out of fear, even with false words (Psalm 18:45; 66:3).

decisions.choice: you will tread on their high places: you will march over their heights in victory
alternatives: you will tread on their backs
you will trample their places of worship
decisions.reason: The word means high ground, the hills that a conqueror holds (32:13; Amos 4:13; Habakkuk 3:19). It can also mean the back or body, picturing a victor setting his foot on the defeated (Joshua 10:24), and it is the word for the hilltop shrines Israel was told to destroy (12:2). The picture is of complete victory; which sense is meant is not certain.

decisions.choice: the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: The double quotation mark opened at verse 2 closes here, at the end of the Blessing.

decisions.choice: He is
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the LORD the subject of a new sentence, so that it is clear who is the shield and the sword.
